panels.rationale: Single substantial hematoxylin-and-eosin histopathology image from a Hailey-Hailey disease article, showing the characteristic dilapidated brick-wall pattern of epidermal acantholysis.
panels.attribution_text: Porro et al. Hailey-Hailey disease: clinical, diagnostic and therapeutic update.. Anais brasileiros de dermatologia 2024. doi:10.1016/j.abd.2023.12.003. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 11.
panels.figure_caption: Presence of acantholytic cells filling the cavity and giving the appearance of a dilapidated brick wall (Hematoxylin & eosin, ×400).
in_text_mentions: nding is marked acantholysis, interspersed with dyskeratotic cells (Fig. 10B), loosely joined, giving the appearance of a “dilapidated brick wall” (also described as an “unplastered wall” as shown in Fig. 11). This acantholysis usually affects the epidermis and spares the adnexal epithelia, which helps in the differential diagnosis with pemphigus vulgaris, where acantholysis affects all epithelia.24 Sometimes eosinophilic compact hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis and acanthosis can also be observed.
